story: On a sunny Monday morning at 11:17, Gary, Donna, and Rosa stand together on Magnolia Loop, trading plans for the parade cart and a Halloween float while the afternoon warms up to 75 degrees. Gary has filed his wiring sketches with Architectural Review and wants Rosa's hospital theme lighting details so he can build it right, and Donna offers him pickleball lessons on her court. Rosa suggests planning sessions on Tuesday and Thursday evenings at her porch around her shifts, and Hal sits watchfully in his porch chair at Hal's House, keeping an eye on the whole Loop.
events: Hal (hal porch chair): Settle into the porch chair and keep an eye on the Loop

gary.thought_process: Donna and Rosa just walked up on Magnolia Loop. Rosa's hospital theme is what's driving my wiring plans, and I've got the sketches tidied up and an Architectural Review application filed. Nobody has said anything yet this tick, so I shouldn't pile on questions. A friendly opener that gets Rosa talking about the parade and shows I'm keeping the cart parked until approval fits who I am and keeps me useful. Donna's flamingos are right there too, so I can tease her lightly and keep it neighborly.

parameters.content: Morning, Rosa, Donna. I got my wiring sketches cleaned up for the parade cart, and I filed with Architectural Review, so she's staying in the garage till they say go. Rosa, I'd love to hear what your hospital theme needs from the lights, so I build it right.

donna.thought_process: Gary and Rosa just arrived on the Loop, and I texted Gary about a practice time and Halloween carts but haven't heard back. He's right here, so I should just ask him in person rather than texting again. My goal is to get him on the pickleball court as my doubles partner, and he's never played. Keep it warm and easy, mention the cart plans going through Architectural Review so Hal stays happy, and don't repeat anything I've already said.

parameters.content: Gary, perfect timing! I've got a court for two hours this week. Don't worry, you'll pick up pickleball in no time. When are you free? Then we can sketch out our Halloween cart plans after.

hal.thought_process: It's late morning, no one's around, and I've already logged the baseline count and scanned the Loop twice. The only thing left on my porch is the chair, and a man can only squint through binoculars so long. Halloween decorations haven't gone up yet, and nothing's violating L-01 or L-02 right now. Patience is the job: sit, watch, and be ready to write it down when somebody gets creative with a flamingo or a cart. Gary and Donna have been behaving lately, and I'll admit I don't mind it.

parameters.content: Settle into the porch chair and keep an eye on the Loop

rosa.thought_process: The welcome dinner went well and Hal is on board, or at least softer. Now Gary and Donna are here on the Loop at the same moment, and the Halloween parade is the next real thing to build. I shouldn't repeat dinner talk. Concrete step: I've penciled in Tuesday and Thursday evenings around my shifts, so I should lock that in with both of them before they wander off. Keep it short and practical, and mention keeping the carts within the rules so Hal's notebook stays quiet.

parameters.content: Donna, Gary, perfect timing. I can do parade planning Tuesday and Thursday evenings around my shifts. Can we do my porch at six, and bring cart ideas that pass review?

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
